issue.body:
# Bug report

### Bug description:

PoC:
```python
import bdb
code = 'a = 1\nb = 2\nc = a + b'
globals_dict = {}
locals_dict = {}
debugger = bdb.Bdb()
debugger.runctx(code, globals_dict, locals_dict)
for i in range(10):
    pass
with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile() as tmpfile:
    tmpfile.seek(0)
```

Config: `--enable-experimental-jit=yes --with-address-sanitizer`

Nevermind, I managed to reproduce it if run as a script instead the REPL:

```py
import base64
empty_encoded = base64.a85encode(b'')
empty_encded
```

Changing `a85encode` to `b64encode` doesn't seem to work so the JIT-ification seems to be important here. However, changing it to `b85encode` also produces a crash. I'll investigate.

To be clear, we also have a simple leak without address sanitizer:

```console
$ ./configure --with-pydebug -q CC=clang --enable-experimental-jit=yes
$ make -s -j12 
$ ./python -X dev -X showrefcount crash.py
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "[...]/cpython/crash.py", line 3, in <module>
    empty_encded
NameError: name 'empty_encded' is not defined. Did you mean: 'empty_encoded'?
[2 refs, 1 blocks]
``` 

So we're indeed having a leak somewhere. I think the executors are not properly cleaned so I'll investigate. The contents of `crash.py` are:

```py
import base64
empty_encoded = base64.b85encode(b'')
empty_encded
```

Yeah, I don't think NameError is important here. I think the deallocation process of executors misses one. valgrind also confirms that the definitely lost bytes come from the executor allocation.
I think maybe the leak is related to https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/e7b55f564dbf5a788e8f6edc55ef441d6afad01c
Actually, deallocation never occurs :') `uop_dealloc` is never called.
The fact that the cold executor is actually immortal may also play a role here.

> The fact that the cold executor is actually immortal may also play a role here.

Yes, I think @brandtbucher has remind about this. FYI https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/136411#discussion_r2244853104

Now, maybe we need some suggestions from @markshannon and @brandtbucher
BTW, I think the sanitizer error is early than #136411

For this script

```python
import base64
empty_encoded = base64.b85encode(b'')
empty_encode
```

The crash is introduced in #133287
Yes, I'm currently modifying this.

Ok to summarize, we currently have the following:

- A cold immortal executor. All executors have references to that cold executor when they are allocated.
- Each threadstate has a referenc to the current executor.
- When we clear exit data, we set the exit data's current executor to the cold executor.

I think the only leak is actually the cold executor but I can't seem to find a way to clear it properly. Created executors are cleared by `executor_clear` but without `uop_dealloc` being ever called. So it's called differently.

I'm not sure I'm right. It seems we actually have issue here

1. the reference leak in #136411. But it will not be the root cause for sanitizer error
2. the sanitizer error in #133287. Seems executor leak here?

The sanitizer error is likely due to a leak, or maybe there are multiple ones. What I could infer is that an executor is never garbage collected. Even changing the cold executor to a non-immortal object, I still have leaks. It may also be because when clearing an executor we're setting its exits executors to the cold executor.

I need more time for this one, probably by changing the entire executor lifecycle logic (we have clears, deallocs, detachs, etc a bit everywhere) since it's hard to see which reference is moved where (though I have some idea). The traversing logic  may also need an update but I won't have time for today. I'll continue tomorrow and hopefully we can make it before 3.14.0 happens (which is in 3 days).

For now, I'm marking it as a release blocker because I don't know if such leaks are actually fine in 3.14.0 for now as it's an experimental feature. Otherwise, we can fix this in 3.14.1.
cc @hugovk
@picnixz Actually, I prefer to release the patch in 3.14.1. JIT is still an experimental feature.
That's my idea as well, but I want the RM decision here.
JIT bugs have never been a release blocker. Removing release blocker label.
I think this is partially also reported in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/137007. However, the repro here is way better, so I'm keeping this issue open.
Should we close 137007? because I don't like having multiple issues open (or we can mark this one as a parent issue of 137007). This issue was specifically for the cold executors used in side exits.
It can't be reproduced on the main branch. Since https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/137007 has been closed, I believe this issue can be closed as well.
